summary: Source-anchored research for Query shape and queryShapeHash stability. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Studio 3T documentation describes its Query hash column using system.profile.queryHash. On MongoDB 8.0+, profiler entries also carry queryShapeHash, a separate field from queryHash/planCacheShapeHash, so treat the field name as part of the grouping definition when comparing tooling. Sources: https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/desktop-ide/mongodb-query-performance/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md

Studio 3T's documentation describes grouping by Exact query using field names and values, and by Query shape using logical structure while ignoring values. That page specifically identifies system.profile.queryHash as its grouping hash; it does not establish that the displayed Query hash is MongoDB's newer queryShapeHash. (medium confidence)

The MongoDB repository describes replacing literals with canonical BSON-type representatives when hashing. Its examples give numeric predicates with different values the same shape, but distinguish a numeric predicate from a string predicate on the same field. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For migration workflows, MongoDB advises verifying that a query shape hash still matches in the target deployment before relying on it. Percona's procedure for migrating Persistent Query Settings uses the representativeQuery field to identify the query when the exported setting has one, and falls back to queryShapeHash otherwise. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/pqs.html

SERVER-93622 records divergent queryShapeHash values and duplicate query-settings entries when repeatedly setting the same representative aggregate query containing $merge and let variables. The historical issue lists fixes in 8.0.4 and 8.1.0-rc0; it is evidence of a past exception, not proof that current versions remain affected. (low confidence)

Percona's ClusterSync migration guide instructs operators to reapply query settings using representativeQuery when present and otherwise use queryShapeHash. Its fallback needs MongoDB's separate target-hash verification guidance before cross-cluster reuse. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/pqs.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md

Shape grouping abstracts literal values: structurally identical commands such as findOne({x:24}) and findOne({x:53}) share a shape, though literals of different BSON types give distinct shapes. Studio 3T's Query Profiler documents this distinction as grouping by Query shape versus Exact query. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/query_shape/README.md ; https://studio3t.com/whats-new/release-2023-9/

Before reusing queryShapeHash across clusters, MongoDB versions, or after a migration, verify that it still matches in the target deployment. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md

MongoDB 8.0 renamed the older queryHash to planCacheShapeHash and introduced the broader queryShapeHash. Percona profiler output shows all three fields, with queryHash equal to planCacheShapeHash and different from queryShapeHash. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/

The documented expectation is that a shape produces the same queryShapeHash across deployment nodes and across replica-set and sharded deployment types. The documentation still requires checking the target hash across clusters, MongoDB versions, and migrations. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Profiler records can expose queryShapeHash for shape-based grouping. MongoDB documents profiler output as a source for the hash, and Percona supplies a concrete profiler record containing it. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/

SERVER-93881 introduced repeated-command explain checks expecting equal queryShapeHash values and links the $merge/let stability bug. These tests support repeatability checks; they do not establish an unconditional compatibility guarantee for every future release. (low confidence)

The find command IDL defines internal originalQueryShapeHash as the hash of the first query entering the query system; its example preserves the router-observed query hash on a shard request. The internal stability annotation is not a public API guarantee. (low confidence)

Query shape normalization groups commands that differ only in literal values into one shape, while Percona describes uneven data distribution leaving a cached plan inefficient, so that it is invalidated and replanned. Queries sharing a shape can therefore differ in execution cost, so compare execution metrics as well as identifiers (this last conclusion is an inference from the two sources, not stated by either). Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/query_shape/README.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/

A query shape includes structural specifications such as filter, sort, projection, namespace, and aggregation pipeline stages. Changing a literal value can preserve the shape; changing the sort field or namespace can change it. (high confidence)

MongoDB 8.0 introduced a broader query-shape model. The pre-existing shape was renamed plan cache query shape, and queryHash was renamed planCacheShapeHash; queryShapeHash identifies the newer model and is a different field. (high confidence)
